gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours each candidate runs the Mini from its one 100 W+ USB-C port, worked out from a measured figure (Wireless Moves ran the Mini for 2 h 45 min on a 72 Wh bank, so it used 26.2 Wh of rated capacity per hour), or that the second USB-C port on the UGREEN 145W bank (65 W) and on the Anker C1000 Gen 2 (shares 20 W with USB-A) can't run the Mini at all.
standout_why: I compared against ChatGPT's answer and the Starlink help pages it cited (a7fe6525 'How can I power my Starlink Mini?' and fba85643 'What USB power rating do I need'), plus the result-14 Mini accessories PDF. The help pages load their text by script and came back empty, and the PDF arrived as compressed binary, so I couldn't read what they say. ChatGPT's answer gives a 100 W PD minimum and a generic runtime table (30 W average with an assumed 85% efficiency, so 100 Wh = 2.8 h). It warns in general terms to check for 100 W 'from a single USB-C port'. It names no products, has no measured runtime, and doesn't say which port on a given product works.
decides: Runtime: at the measured 26.2 Wh per hour, a 90 Wh bank (UGREEN 145W) gives about 3.4 h, enough for an evening but not a day. A 1 kWh LiFePO4 station gives about 39 h from USB-C alone. The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 costs least per hour of runtime ($12.8/h) and has about the same Wh per lb as the Anker C1000 Gen 2. The Elite 30 V2 (about 11 h, 9.5 lb, $299.99) suits one night of camping. Ports: on the UGREEN 145W the Mini must go in USB-C1 (140 W), and on the C1000 Gen 2 in USB-C2 (140 W). The other USB-C port on each is under 100 W, and Wireless Moves saw a 60 W bank put the Mini into a boot loop.

findings.label: Starlink Mini measured average draw
findings.value: 21 W average; 21–40 W range; 40 W and higher only in the first 1–2 minutes after power-on
findings.source_title: Starlink Mini – Part 2 – Power and Performance (Wireless Moves)
findings.note: Measured by Wireless Moves on an Anker power station.

findings.label: Measured Mini runtime on a USB-C PD power bank
findings.value: 2 h 45 min on a 72 Wh, 500 g, 100 W PD bank, which is 26.2 Wh of rated capacity per hour
findings.source_title: Starlink Mini – Part 2 – Power and Performance (Wireless Moves)
findings.note: 72 Wh ÷ 2.75 h = 26.2 Wh/h. That equals 21 W × 2.75 h / 72 Wh = 80% of rated Wh delivered. The same article says a 60 W bank caused a boot loop and a 100 W PD bank worked. I use 26.2 Wh/h as the divisor for every runtime below. That is an assumption for the stations, whose USB-C conversion losses weren't measured.

unsourced: Text of Starlink's own Mini help pages (a7fe6525, fba85643), specifications page and the accessories_guide_mini.pdf / specification_sheet_mini.pdf. The pages render by script and WebFetch returned only 'Starlink'. The PDFs came back as compressed binary, and running pdftotext needed a permission I don't have. So I couldn't quote Starlink's own average-draw or 100 W wording.
UGREEN 145W 25000mAh weight: the product page returned HTTP 429 twice, so I couldn't compute Wh per lb or hours per lb for it.
Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 US price today: ankersolix.com showed no dollar amount and isn't a Shopify store storecheck can read. I skipped Amazon given the call budget.

EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus main unit: neither storecheck search nor the product URL found it on us.ecoflow.com (404; only the extra battery is listed at $149), and the WebFetch attempt hit HTTP 429. I didn't derive price, weight or hours for it.
Baseus Blade H1 100W and AOHi Starship 40000mAh: storecheck returned HTTP 404 for both stores.
A measured USB-C output efficiency for any power station (as opposed to a power bank). The 26.2 Wh/h divisor comes from a power bank test and is applied to the stations as an assumption.
